transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Sofia Duarte (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (NorthStar Head of Data), Marcus Feld (VP Eng), Asha Singh (Security Architect), Tom Riley (Platform Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be fuzzy):
NorthStar wants to understand Redwood hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), deep dive on security posture: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and Okta integration, RBAC and audit logging, encryption + KMS/BYOK, data retention/deletion policy, and feasibility of a pilot with their live-ish data. Agreed to send SOC2 docs and schedule pilot benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: hey everyone thanks for joining — i'm ethan from redwood, i'm the ae on the account, and with me is sofia our se. how are you all?
[00:12] Laura Kim: hi thanks — all good here. we put a quick agenda in the invite but mostly it's about security posture and how you'd host critical models for fund analytics.
[00:23] Sofia Duarte: great, yeah we'll run through hosted, dedicated, private options and then dive into your compliance checklist. quick note — transcript may have a few errors, names sometimes scrambled.
[00:35] Marcus Feld: that's fine. start with a high-level — what certs and audits do you have? our security team needs SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 coverage ideally.
[00:44] Ethan Morales: sure, we have SOC2 Type II — i'll send the report after the call. we also maintain an iso 27001 mapping doc, and we do pen tests annually. i'll include links to the certs, sorry i mean attachments [link: redwood_SOC2_2025.pdf] and [link: iso27001_mapping.xlsx].
[01:05] Asha Singh: okay cool. does your hosted offering allow us to use our KMS keys? we need BYOK for some datasets.
[01:13] Sofia Duarte: short answer: yes for Private and in many Dedicated configurations — we support external KMS (customer-managed keys) via HSM/KMS integrations. for Hosted API we offer envelope encryption and we manage keys by default, but we can do a partner-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated/Private deployments. there are some handshake steps for key rotation and access patterns.
[01:40] Tom Riley: hmm, can you elaborate on the handshake? we have strict key rotation policies. does rotation trigger downtime or cache invalidation for long-running sessions?
[01:49] Sofia Duarte: good question. the runtime supports key rotation without shredding the model state; you need to call the rotation API and rotate the master-wrapping key — kv cache and tokenization keys are handled separately. there can be a short window for re-encryption of persisted artifacts, but we do streaming re-wrap to avoid long downtimes. i'll capture the exact steps in the doc i send.
[02:12] Marcus Feld: and audit logs — what level of granularity? we need per-request identifiers, who accessed which route, and retention for 12 months minimum.
[02:21] Ethan Morales: we emit detailed audit logs with request id, route, model version, user id (if provided), and latency/cost metadata. logs can be pushed to your SIEM (splunk, sentinel) via syslog or cloud forwarders. retention is configurable — on Hosted we have default retention policies, Dedicated/Private you control retention in your storage.
[02:44] Laura Kim: does redwood support SSO? we use okta, need SAML and scim for provisioning.
[02:51] Sofia Duarte: yes — SSO via SAML/Okta is supported across Console and API auth flows. we also support SCIM for user provisioning, and we have role-based access controls — RBAC is pluggable with custom roles. note: for some private deployments we integrate with your internal IdP directly.
[03:12] Asha Singh: on RBAC, can we enforce per-team usage quotas and per-route overrides? also need separation of duties for ops vs security.
[03:22] Sofia Duarte: yes you can create roles with route-level permissions and token-scoped quotas. we also support org-level policies and can restrict create/delete model actions to specific roles. separation of duties is supported via our fine-grained roles and audit trails.
[03:40] Marcus Feld: do you have SOC2 logs for the console and api calls separate? we need proof that console actions are audited.
[03:47] Ethan Morales: yes, the SOC2 scope covers console and API actions; i'll flag the relevant sections in the report.
[03:53] Laura Kim: data residency — can you pin data to eu-west-1? we're partly in eu and must keep certain datasets in region.
[04:02] Sofia Duarte: absolutely, we support region pinning for Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted tier has region controls but with shared infra. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can pin model serving and logs to a specific cloud region.
[04:18] Tom Riley: what's the difference cost/latency-wise between Dedicated and Private on-prem?
[04:24] Sofia Duarte: Dedicated is redwood-hosted reserved GPU pools in your cloud region with predictable throughput and comes with SLAs. Private is either VPC-hosted with customer-managed control plane or full on-prem. Private typically has higher setup and support fees but gives you full network control and lower egress latency if it's on-prem. Dedicated is quicker to launch. we'll include a cost comparator.
[04:46] Marcus Feld: for our quant workloads, we need to measure p99 latency at 2k tokens. can you do a pilot?
[04:53] Sofia Duarte: yes — we can run a benchmark on Dedicated nodes or Private staging. we recommend Dedicated for the initial pilot because it's fastest to provision. we'll need sample payloads and expected concurrency.
[05:07] Laura Kim: about retention/deletion — how do you handle user-requested deletions? do you have end-to-end deletion, and can we prove it?
[05:15] Ethan Morales: we handle deletion at multiple layers: request logs, cache, persisted payloads. for Hosted we have documented deletion flows and can provide deletion proofs (audit artifacts). for Dedicated/Private you control the storage so you can implement deletion policies yourself; we provide APIs and runbooks for secure deletion.
[05:34] Asha Singh: any details on immutable audit logs? our compliance team wants tamper-evident logs for at least 12 months.
[05:41] Sofia Duarte: we can ship logs to WORM storage or to your SIEM with write-once policies. we also support signed log entries with trunked hashes you can validate. i'll attach an architecture note.
[05:58] Marcus Feld: ransomware threats — do you have a threat model and DR runbooks?
[06:04] Ethan Morales: yes, we publish incident response and DR playbooks; we also do tabletop exercises with enterprise customers as part of the onboarding. i'll share the summary doc.
[06:14] Tom Riley: what's the network model for private? is it VPC peering, transit gateway, or direct connect?
[06:20] Sofia Duarte: we support VPC peering, transit gateway, and direct connect. Private deployments can be either customer-managed VPC with a control plane in their cloud, or air-gapped on-prem. we'll include sample network diagrams.
[06:35] Laura Kim: can we get a signed DPA and addenda for financial data?
[06:40] Ethan Morales: yes, we have a standard DPA with financial addendum. legal can start redlining once we send initial documents.
[06:48] Marcus Feld: any gaps we should know about? like certs you don't have, or processes still in progress?
[06:54] Ethan Morales: we're SOC2 Type II and have ISO mappings; some customers require FedRAMP or specific country-level certifications which we don't have by default. if you need those we can discuss partners or on-prem solutions to meet controls.
[07:10] Asha Singh: encryption at rest — is everything encrypted by default? and for embeddings/LLM state?
[07:16] Sofia Duarte: yes, encryption at rest is default in Hosted; for embeddings and model state we encrypt ephemeral caches and persisted checkpoints; in Dedicated/Private you choose key control. the model weights are usually in read-only buckets and wrapped with envelope encryption.
[07:33] Marcus Feld: any limits on logs export size or ingestion? we have high-volume telemetry.
[07:38] Sofia Duarte: logging pipeline is scalable but for very high throughput we recommend pushing logs to your storage/SIEM — we can set up high-throughput forwarders. retention/ingestion limits are configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[07:52] Laura Kim: question on SAML: can you force re-auth every X hours for sensitive workflows?
[07:57] Sofia Duarte: yes session TTLs and MFA policies are enforced via your IdP; we honor SAML session settings and can also enforce token TTLs on the Redwood side.
[08:10] Tom Riley: performance isolation — if we run a dedicated node pool, will noisy neighbors be an issue?
[08:16] Sofia Duarte: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools; we do per-customer scheduling and preemptive reservations to avoid noisy neighbor effects. for extra isolation you can go Private single-tenant.
[08:27] Marcus Feld: what telemetry do we get for cost breakdown? tokens, model version, route?
[08:32] Ethan Morales: you get token-level cost attribution, per-route breakdowns, and per-model version metrics. console exports to csv and to BI pipelines. we'll include sample dashboard screenshots.
[08:46] Laura Kim: ok can we recap the things you said you'd send?
[08:50] Ethan Morales: yes — SOC2 and ISO docs, network diagrams and VPC whitepaper, benchmark plan, draft SOW, DPA, and the audit/logging architecture note.
[08:58] Asha Singh: for the benchmark, we need an NDA for sample data. do you have a standard NDA or do we share ours?
[09:05] Ethan Morales: we have a standard NDA; if you prefer to share yours we can sign that too. i'll attach our NDA in the follow-ups.
[09:14] Marcus Feld: timeline — if everything lines up, we want a pilot in 2–3 weeks. is that feasible?
[09:20] Sofia Duarte: feasible for Dedicated; for Private it depends on network approvals. we'll aim for 2 weeks to stand up a Dedicated pilot if you provide data samples and credentials for the benchmark.
[09:33] Laura Kim: any cost ballpark for the pilot?
[09:37] Ethan Morales: we'll provide an estimate in the SOW; pilot cost typically covers reserved nodes for the pilot duration and engineering hours for onboarding.
[09:44] Tom Riley: are there any special SOC2 items around model change control? our auditors want to see model update logs and who approved rollouts.
[09:52] Sofia Duarte: yes, our platform records model publish events, who triggered them, and we support canary rollouts with approval gates — those are part of the audit trail. we'll call out the model change control section in the SOC2 map.
[10:06] Marcus Feld: ok — on the technical side, can the runtime run on bare-metal gpu or does it need certain kernel modules?
[10:13] Sofia Duarte: we support popular GPU instances and bare-metal; some kernel modules and drivers must match the runtime requirements — we'll send a hardware checklist for Private/on-prem.
[10:24] Laura Kim: are backups encrypted and do you have periodic restore tests?
[10:29] Sofia Duarte: yes backups are encrypted and we do scheduled restore drills; frequency depends on deployment.
[10:34] Ethan Morales: alright let me go over next steps and action items to be explicit — i'll email the docs: SOC2, ISO mapping, NDA, DPA, VPC diagram, benchmark plan, and draft SOW. sofia will schedule the benchmark and provide the hardware checklist.
[10:52] Asha Singh: that's good. also please include the list of log fields you surface in the audit export — we want to validate against our SIEM schema.
[11:01] Sofia Duarte: noted — i'll attach a sample log schema (json lines) and a sample SIEM mapping.
[11:10] Marcus Feld: final quick Q — do you have an official retention policy template we can use to set our policies?
[11:16] Ethan Morales: yes, retention templates and policy docs will be included. for Hosted there are defaults; Dedicated/Private you fully control retention.
[11:26] Tom Riley: thanks — we'll review and get back with a final list of regulatory controls.
[11:31] Laura Kim: thanks all.
[11:33] Ethan Morales: thanks everybody; we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed times for the benchmark.

End of recording.
